what: Platform-pack event mnemonics, as data: per config dialect, the syslog mnemonics that record the events a person asks about (a reload, a restart, an interface or line protocol going up or down, an OSPF or BGP adjacency changing, the configuration changed), each with what it records and the words a question says it with. Ask in words offers them for every question, beside the mnemonics the logs reader counted, so an event the range happens not to hold is still named (the operator's walk, 2026-10-26: "Which devices rebooted this week?" was filled with the text "reboot", which IOS never logs).
how: Mnemonics as the logs builder carries them (%FACILITY-SEVERITY-NAME), spelled as Cisco's IOS and IOS-XE system message guides give them; %SYS-5-RELOAD, %OSPF-5-ADJCHG, %LINK-3-UPDOWN and %SYS-5-CONFIG_I are also in the lab's Loki (the operator's walk and the logs builder's presets, 2026-10-26). A reload logs %SYS-5-RELOAD when it is asked for and %SYS-5-RESTART when the system comes back. The words are lower-case, matched as Ask in words matches a question's words. OSPFv3's %OSPFv3-5-ADJCHG is left out until the logs builder takes its lower-case v (C1813).

cisco_ios.records: a reload was requested (the device is about to restart)
the system restarted (logged as it comes back up)
an interface changed state to up or down
an interface's line protocol changed state to up or down
an OSPF neighbour's adjacency changed state
a BGP neighbour went up or down
the configuration was changed (by whom, from where)
